strategies.title: Habit strategies
strategies.entryHint_one: {{count}} tried way to build a habit
strategies.entryHint_other: {{count}} tried ways to build a habit
strategies.lead: Start with one idea and make it part of your habit.
strategies.remindA11y: Remind me of “{{title}}” once a week
strategies.reminderOn: You will be reminded of it once a week.

start-tiny.idea: Start with an amount so small it needs no effort.
start-tiny.example: Two minutes of Quran instead of a whole juz.
start-tiny.ask: What is the smallest amount of {{habit}} you will start with?
start-tiny.suggest: I start with just {{amount}}, and add nothing until it settles.

anchor-prayer.idea: Place the habit after a set prayer, so the prayer reminds you of it.
anchor-prayer.example: The adhkar right after the Fajr prayer.
anchor-prayer.ask: After which prayer will you do {{habit}}?
anchor-prayer.suggest: Right after the {{prayer}} prayer, where I pray.

if-then.idea: Decide in advance what you will do when the moment comes.
if-then.example: If I miss my wird, then I will read one page before sleep.
if-then.ask: If {{habit}} slips past its time, what will you do?
if-then.suggest: If it slips past its time, then before I sleep I do my minimum: {{amount}}.

prepare-place.idea: Set out what the habit needs before its time.
prepare-place.example: The mushaf on the desk, the prayer mat laid out.
prepare-place.ask: What will you set out for {{habit}} before its time, and where?

block-sin.idea: Keep the means of the sin out of reach, and make the way to it long.
block-sin.example: Delete the app, and leave the phone outside the room at night.

never-twice.idea: If you miss the habit one day, do not miss it a second day.
never-twice.example: After a missed day, start your day with its smallest amount.

make-up.idea: What you did not finish yesterday, finish before noon today, and it counts for its day.
make-up.example: You missed your night wird, so read it in the forenoon.
make-up.ask: If you miss {{habit}} one day, when will you finish it?
make-up.suggest: If I miss a day, I finish it the next morning, before noon.

bundle.idea: Pair the habit with something you enjoy and look forward to.
bundle.example: I read my wird with the morning coffee I enjoy.
bundle.ask: What do you enjoy that you will pair with {{habit}}?

season.idea: Seasons of good help a start; hearts are more willing in them.
season.example: Begin fasting Mondays and Thursdays in Shaban.

know-weak.idea: Notice the time, place and state in which you weaken.
know-weak.example: After midnight, when you are alone.

ride-wave.idea: An urge rises and then falls; hold on for a few minutes.
ride-wave.example: Make wudu, or change your place for ten minutes.

follow-good.idea: If you slip, repent, and follow the slip with a good deed at once.
follow-good.example: A small charity or two rakahs after the slip.

company.idea: Keep company that helps you to good, and look in on your friends.
company.example: Agree with a friend on a shared wird.

self-review.idea: Take a minute each evening: what did you keep, and what did you miss?

strategies.deedsLead: Easy good deeds with a great reward. Open one, or make it a habit.

cue.label: The cue
cue.question: When and where does it start?
cue.hint: Tie it to something that happens every day: a prayer, a place, a usual act.

craving.label: The intention
craving.question: What do you want from it?
craving.hint: A clear intention renews the wish each time.

routine.label: The act
routine.question: What exactly do you do?
routine.hint: A small, precise act that is easy to begin.

reward.label: The reward
reward.question: What do you find after it?

aboutPage.lead: Every book named, every narration graded.
aboutPage.intro: Thekra cites the book and the person who graded a narration. A book is never given one grade for every hadith in it.
aboutPage.methodologyBody: Every text names its source. A verse shows its surah and ayah; a hadith shows its book, number, and the grade given by the authority that graded it. Quoted words stay distinct from any explanation Thekra adds.
aboutPage.openitiBody: Digital texts imported from OpenITI are used under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 licence. Attribution: OpenITI. Thekra does not sell this text and does not run ads on it. If the dataset is shared, it stays under the same licence.

heart.title: For one who has a heart
heart.line: Habits that revive the heart, a program that lightens it, and the branches of faith.

listening.title: Or gives ear
listening.line: One text at a time, one task per page, and few notifications.

presence.title: While present
presence.line: A present heart and honest self-review, with no points, ranks or comparisons.

aboutPage.eyebrow: Thekra, for whoever has a heart
aboutPage.privacyBody: Your habits are kept in your account; “Lighten” is encrypted so no one else can read it, and no notification names it. Logging is for reminding and following up; acceptance is with Allah.
aboutPage.more: The full methodology on the website
